title: Humanoid Showroom Assistant: Simulation-First Autonomy
summary: LLM-driven showroom assistant on the Unitree G1 featuring simulation-first autonomy, Isaac Sim digital twins, and safety-critical HAL architecture.
problem: Showroom and customer exhibition spaces are dynamic, unstructured environments with visitors, varying lighting, and fragile surroundings. Demonstrating advanced humanoid capabilities requires interactive dialogue, reliable station-to-station navigation, and expressive gestures without risking human safety or physical hardware damage.
approach: Engineered a simulation-first architecture in NVIDIA Isaac Sim coupled with a robot-agnostic ROS 2 Hardware Abstraction Layer (HAL). Integrated an LLM conversational engine with behavior tree orchestration, 3D workspace safety zones, and staged physical deployment on the Unitree G1.
implementation: Modular 4-layer software stack decoupling high-level autonomy from robot-specific runtime adapters
Isaac Sim digital twin environment replicating showroom presentation stations and physical kinematics
HARA-based safety framework with 3D workspace boundaries, command rate adaptation, and watchdog interlocks
LLM speech interaction pipeline integrated with synchronized upper-body presentation gestures
Nav2 station-to-station autonomous waypoint navigation with dynamic human proximity buffers
Staged sim-to-real transfer procedure validating stability, timing, and safety triggers prior to live tests

results.evidence: Simulated showroom environment with kinematic and dynamic validation in Isaac Sim.
Decoupled autonomy, digital twin, ROS 2 middleware/HAL, and robot runtime adapters.
Target platform with Inspire dexterous hands configured via standardized ROS 2 topics.
Progressive validation protocol with hardware watchdogs and risk-based emergency stop logic.

caseStudy.systemArchitecture: Built on a modular 4-layer architecture. Autonomy applications (LLM speech interaction, behavior tree orchestration, and Nav2 waypoint navigation) interface through a standardized Hardware Abstraction Layer (HAL). This architecture ensures high-level application logic remains independent of physical robot hardware, enabling identical code execution in simulation and on the real Unitree G1.
caseStudy.safetyDesign: Developed using Hazard Analysis and Risk Assessment (HARA) principles. Features multi-tier safety: 3D workspace bounding boxes limiting arm and torso extensions, manipulation velocity and acceleration clamps, command-rate adaptation to prevent actuator shock, hardware watchdogs monitoring joint temperatures and communication heartbeats, and a deterministic risk-based emergency-stop state machine falling back to safe damping postures upon anomaly detection.
caseStudy.simulationValidation: Established a simulation-first development workflow in NVIDIA Isaac Sim. Recreated digital twins of the showroom environment, sensor configurations, and the Unitree G1 kinematics. Verified path planning, presentation timing, workspace boundaries, and fail-safe triggers across hundreds of simulated trials before deploying to physical hardware.
demoCapabilities: LLM-powered conversational interaction answering visitor inquiries on technical topics
Autonomous waypoint navigation guiding guests between multiple showroom presentation stations
Expressive, synchronized upper-body gestures during spoken presentations
Real-time environmental reaction pausing locomotion or gestures if visitors enter proximity buffers
Digital twin synchronized monitoring visualizing real-time robot telemetry
engineeringLearnings: Decoupling autonomy from hardware through a strict HAL reduced integration iteration time by over 50%
Simulation-first validation in Isaac Sim exposed edge-case joint limit violations that would have caused hardware trips on the physical robot
LLM interaction requires structured response streaming and state timeouts to prevent dialogue latency from stalling physical behavior trees
Staged physical validation with progressive safety envelopes is critical when bringing experimental bipedal platforms into human environments

title: Multi-Stream Video Analytics Platform
summary: Real-time counting, tracking, and SKU classification across 4 concurrent RTSP camera feeds with 99.2% validation accuracy under controlled illumination.
problem: Real-time inventory and sorting tracking across 4 high-speed processing lines was manual, labor-intensive, and prone to 25%+ count discrepancies. The system required multi-stream ingestion with sub-50ms latency per frame.
approach: Built GPU-accelerated multi-stream pipeline using NVIDIA DeepStream SDK. Custom YOLO model trained on 8,000+ domain images, optimized via TensorRT engine for 50% inference latency reduction.
implementation: 4-camera RTSP ingestion pipeline with automated reconnect & failover
YOLOv5 / v8 object detection with secondary classifier for item sub-categorization
TensorRT FP16 serialization for sub-45ms multi-stream inference
Kafka message bus streaming metrics to TimescaleDB and real-time dashboard
REST APIs serving analytics to factory line managers

results.evidence: Evaluated on 5,000 annotated conveyor frames across 4 synchronized cameras under controlled industrial lighting.
Profiled via NVIDIA Nsight Systems on Jetson AGX Xavier running TensorRT FP16/INT8.
Decoded directly into NVMM unified memory via NVIDIA DeepStream SDK.
Facility operational transition from 5 manual stations down to 2 oversight operators.

title: Autonomous Robotic Waste Sorting System
summary: End-to-end vision-guided robotic picking cell with multi-robot coordination sorting 10,000+ objects daily.
problem: Conveyor belt waste sorting requires continuous operation under severe visual occlusion, shifting object shapes, and variable conveyor speeds without dropping cycle times.
approach: Engineered an overhead high-speed camera setup coupled with ROS2 robotic control. Integrated YOLO object detection with 3-axis delta/gantry manipulator motion planning.
implementation: Overhead industrial vision box with synchronized strobe lighting
YOLO object detector tuned for high-speed conveyor belts
ROS2 nodes managing inverse kinematics and conveyor encoder tracking
Refactored trajectory planning from Python to C++ loops for 80% compute reduction
Dynamic pick queue scheduling to optimize multi-arm duty cycles

results.evidence: Ground-truth facility operating log across dual 8-hour industrial waste sorting shifts.
Profiled trajectory planning and post-processing refactored from Python to multithreaded C++20.
Measured on 3-axis gantry picking cell by transitioning from trapezoidal motion profiles to jerk-limited S-curves.
Combined frame capture, inference, motion planning, and pneumatic actuator trigger latency.

title: Robo Café: UR10 Automated Manipulation Cell
summary: Fully automated robotic café with UR10 manipulator on 7th-axis linear rail executing precision pick-and-place.
problem: Exhibition visitors expect continuous automated drink and snack preparation with precise ingredient handling and zero collisions in a shared glass enclosure.
approach: Configured UR10 6-DOF arm mounted on a linear 7th axis. Solved the re-teaching drift problem using fiducial marker-based relative positioning combined with MoveIt motion planning.
implementation: UR10 robot arm integrated with external 7th-axis linear servo rail
MoveIt planning pipeline with collision models for all kitchen equipment
Marker-based camera registration to dynamically compensate for mechanical drift
Omron PLC integration via industrial fieldbus for dispenser trigger signals
Gazebo dynamic simulation to validate workspace envelopes before commissioning

results.evidence: UR10 6-DOF manipulator mounted on 7th-axis linear servo rail.
Pre-deployment Gazebo simulation validated workspace envelopes before physical hardware setup.
Continuous MoveIt collision mesh checking against kitchen equipment and glass barriers.
Fiducial marker camera calibration compensating for linear rail mechanical drift.

title: 4-DOF SCARA Air Hockey Robot with 240 FPS Vision
summary: High-speed competitive robot playing real-time air hockey against human opponents with Kalman trajectory prediction.
problem: Pucks travel across the table in under 300ms with multiple bank-shots. The system must perceive, predict multi-bounce trajectory, plan interception, and command the robot with sub-50ms latency.
approach: 500 FPS overhead camera coupled with OpenCV puck segmentation. Kalman filter continuously estimates 2D velocity vectors and bounces, driving a 4-DOF SCARA arm via Modbus/TCP.
implementation: High-speed overhead camera running at 240+ FPS tracking high-contrast puck
Multi-bounce Kalman filter trajectory prediction with boundary restitution physics
Motion arbiter deciding between block, aggressive strike, and center clear
Direct Modbus/TCP communication to Epson SCARA controller for lowest latency
Interactive PyQt GUI for visitor speed and difficulty calibration

results.evidence: High-speed camera vision loop for real-time trajectory interception on air hockey table.
Kalman filter trajectory estimation executed in C++ within 10ms.
Custom SCARA kinematics controller running on microcontroller hardware.
Measured across 100+ exhibition matches against human opponents.

title: ATOL: Vision-Only 3D Position Estimation
summary: Vision-based automated landing pose estimation system for aircraft where GPS degrades near ground level.
problem: GPS signals can become unreliable or jammed during low-altitude approach and landing phases. Autonomous landing requires continuous, metric-accuracy 3D position relative to runway thresholds.
approach: Vision-only estimation using custom keypoint detection on runway corners fused with PnP stereo estimation and ORB-SLAM3 for metric runway-frame localization.
implementation: Custom YOLOv8-Pose model extracting runway threshold corners and markings
PnP and stereo geometry recovering continuous relative 6-DOF transform
ORB-SLAM3 visual-inertial odometry integration for robust tracking during occlusion
Synthetic flight trajectory validation in Unity / FlightGear simulation environments

title: Store Separation: 6-DOF High-Speed Pose Estimation
summary: Photogrammetry algorithm recovering 6-DOF trajectory of released aircraft stores from high-speed video footage.
problem: Analyzing aerodynamic separation of aircraft payloads previously required tedious frame-by-frame manual tracking with TrackEye, introducing human error and taking weeks per flight test.
approach: Developed an automated photogrammetry and model-based computer vision pipeline matching optical features to 3D CAD geometries, recovering full 6-DOF trajectory.
implementation: High-speed multi-view video ingestion and temporal synchronization
Iterative PnP optimization with CAD silhouette matching
Automated outlier rejection to handle smoke, glint, and aerodynamic vapor
Validation against simulation ground truth and calibrated TrackEye datasets

title: Grinding-Wheel Visual Anomaly Detection
summary: Unsupervised optical QC station flagging microscopic defects on manufactured grinding wheels using Anomalib & DeepStream.
problem: Defects on industrial grinding wheels are varied (cracks, chips, uneven bonding) and good samples vastly outnumber defects, making traditional supervised classifiers unfeasible.
approach: Unsupervised anomaly detection trained solely on defect-free reference wheels using PatchCore and PaDiM. Integrated OCR reads wheel serial numbers for SKU-specific parameter selection.
implementation: PatchCore & PaDiM anomaly localization models trained on non-defective parts
Recentering preprocessing algorithm eliminating false positives from part rotation
OCR model reading stamped alphanumeric codes to look up tolerance profiles
NVIDIA DeepStream multi-camera acceleration for concurrent inspection
TensorRT engine optimization for deterministic cycle times

title: Pepper Humanoid Robot Exhibition Integration
summary: Human-robot interaction framework with face recognition, visitor engagement, and choreographed behaviors.
problem: Stock Pepper behaviors were repetitive and lacked contextual awareness for a museum exhibition with thousands of daily visitors of diverse ages.
approach: Integrated YOLO object detection and face recognition with SoftBank NAOqi SDK. Built an interactive backend routing visitor queries to tailored robotic gestures and dialogues.
implementation: NAOqi SDK interface with custom ROS bridges for sensor access
Real-time face recognition and visitor tracking pipeline
Custom choreographed interaction routines tailored for public demonstration
Web-based kiosk dashboard for docents to control exhibition modes

title: Robo Soccer: Autonomous Multi-Robot Fleet
summary: Autonomous 3v3 robot soccer coordination with centralized overhead computer vision and dynamic tactical role switching.
problem: Coordinating 6 high-speed mobile robots in a dynamic game with rapid changes in possession, collision risks, and strict low-cost robot constraints.
approach: Centralized intelligence architecture: overhead camera tracks color fiducials on all robots and the ball, computes field tactics, and transmits motor commands via RF links.
implementation: Overhead vision tracker with color fiducial identification running at 60 FPS
Dynamic role allocation algorithm (Striker, Defender, Goalkeeper)
Potential field navigation and ball interception vector calculation
Low-latency wireless RF command transmitter communicating with Arduino robots

title: Da Vinci Surgical Robot — Gesture Teleoperation
summary: Retrofitted surgical robotic arms with contactless Leap Motion gesture control for visitor demonstrations.
problem: The multi-million dollar surgical console could not be directly operated by general public visitors due to sanitization and complexity constraints.
approach: Engineered a contactless gesture teleoperation bridge using Leap Motion infrared tracking. Mapped human hand joints to inverse kinematics of the multi-joint surgical manipulators.
implementation: Leap Motion skeletal hand tracking integration with ROS node
Kinematic workspace scaling and safety boundary clamping
Gesture state machine distinguishing between grasp, rotate, and traverse
Arduino Mega hardware interface driving actuator stages

title: Precision Metal Component Optical QC System
summary: Automated defect inspection for precision automotive components measuring sub-100 micron geometric tolerances.
problem: Critical automotive valves required manual microscope inspection to catch burrs, scratches, and pitting. Manual inspection was slow (45s per part) and had 12% escape rates.
approach: Engineered multi-illumination telecentric optical cell with custom CNN defect classifier running on NVIDIA hardware synchronized with industrial PLC line ejector.
implementation: Telecentric optics with structured diffuse dome lighting
Custom CNN segmentation architecture trained on microscopic surface anomalies
NVIDIA Triton inference server providing sub-second part classification
Omron PLC pneumatic ejector integration for automatic reject binning

problem: Sorting variable payload packages across dual workcells without collision or deadlock, while tracking real-time enterprise inventory databases.
approach: Engineered coordinated trajectory planning in MoveIt with MQTT message synchronization. Built an automated order fulfillment pipeline in Gazebo simulation.

MoveIt planning scene synchronization with dynamic collision obstacles
MQTT broker dispatching parallel tasks without robot mutual deadlocks
Automated spreadsheet API integration for order status and logistics logging
